label: text
text: POST-BOYCOTT EFFECT

label: text
text: Although the Boycott and Strike were officially off on Sunday last our market has not responded in fact most of the favourite Industrials show a decline on last week with Sellers prevailing.

label: text
text: Shanghai Market is firm with a good demand for Cottons and Rubbers.

label: text
text: The following are the principal alterations since last week:—

label: text
text: Banks:—Declined to a selling rate of $1,140 at which price sales took place, to-day $1,150 would probably have to be paid to obtain shares.

label: text
text: Unions: — Carne to business at $295/6 and it is doubtful if there are buyers at over the former price.

label: text
text: Canton Insurance and Hong Kong Fires: — Are unchanged with buyers but no sellers.

label: text
text: Trams:—Have sellers at $26 and less would be accepted.

label: text
text: China Sugars:—Are farmer with buyers but no sellers at $24, China: Providers:—Are still wanted, buyers offering $6.10. China Lights:—After a few transactions at $21 for the combined shares are now quoted nominal at $21%.

label: text
text: Steamboats: — Changed hands at $29, at which price there are still buyers but no further sellers.

label: text
text: Hong Kong Lands: —Some business was put through at $643/65, and there are still buyers at the latter price.

label: text
text: Humphreys: — Rose to a buying rate of $16^{th}$ without attracting sellers and they close nominal at this price.

label: text
text: Cements: After sales at $14½ for the combined shares have experienced a decline, $133% having been accepted with buyers now only offering $13.

label: text
text: Wharves:—Firmed up during the week $ ^{1} $ and came to business at 127½; they are still wanted at 127.

label: text
text: Hong Kong „Docks“ — Are a steady with buyers and sales at $58.

label: text
text: Star Ferries:—A few sales took place at $68, but at the close they were easier with sellers at $67½.

label: text
text: Dairy Farms: — After a few sales at $19½/19½ have no further buyers at the moment.

label: text
text: Electrics: -- Were more or less neglected and after a few sales at $67½ close nominal at this price.

label: text
text: London Quotations: — Have undergone no change.

label: text
text: Exchange: Demand rate on London is 1/11 9/16 and T/T on Shanghai is 78%.

label: text
text: Next Settlement Day is Tuesday. October 26.

text: PEKING OR CANTON?

label: paragraph_title
text: (Continued from Page 1.)

label: text
text: ed in a body because they had given up all hope of ever getting any money with which to pay salaries. The teachers in these schools, who have salaries due them since April 1925, met to-day and will appeal to the presidents to reconsider their resignations. They will also send delegations to the new acting Premier, to the Minister of Finance, and to the Minister of Education, but the school problem seems insoluble without millions of dollars on hand—and there are no millions even remotely in sight.

label: text
text: Peking is filled with out-of-town students, and they are now in a distressful condition. The authorities have given them permission to live in the dormitories free for one month, on the slim hope that the schools may be able to open, within 30 days. Most of them, however, have no lights and no water—both services having been cut off because the government could not pay the bills.

label: text
text: The coal situation is admittedly very serious, and if something is not done at once Peking will have not only no heating, but also no power of any kind, no trams and no lights. The Peking Electric Co. has appealed to the Government, and also to General Chang Hsuehliang: (Chang Tso-lin's "son) for cond-cars, and says it will have to close down if fuel is not forthcoming.

label: paragraph_title
text: Military Parasites.

label: text
text: There is excellent coal within 20 miles of Peking at the Menketou mines, but the military have taken all the cars and locomotives, and no reserves have been laid in. Camel transport, or transports by

label: text
text: Coal at the Mentekou mine costs $3 a ton. In Peking, 20 miles away. It costs $18 a ton. A year ago, with the same mine price, Peking paid only $7 a ton.

label: text
text: The militarists tax all goods hauled by rail $4 per ton, and also get a "victory tax" of $25 per car, and an additional tax of $500 for every freight "train of 15 cars." This explains some of the increase in price.

label: text
text: Even many rich people have no coal on hand, with which to heat their homes, and already the mercury is down nearly to 32 every night.

label: text
text: The authorities are making a determined "drive against the "Reds" both here and in Tientsin. Many Cantonese have landed at the latter port, and though scores have been arrested many have managed to reach Peking. "Yesterday, more than 30 of these were put into prison, and it is said that some of them found with incriminating literature will be decapitated. Many arrests have been made also from the personnel of the Peking University.

label: paragraph_title
text: Sneaking to Canton.

label: text
text: An official order has been put out forbidding students here from leaving for universities at Canton. Especially since the Cantonese captured Hankow, Canton propagandists have been busy among the students, and many have sneaked away for Canton. They go disguised as coolies, or as soldiers.

label: text
text: Heads of all schools have been instructed to search dormitories and libraries for Red literature, and the police are destroying all such reading matter that is found.

label: text
text: Chang Tso-lin, from Mukden, has issued an order forbidding the Fengtien troops now controlling Peking from interfering in any way with the civil administration, and from oppressing the merchants or collecting arbitrary taxes.

label: text
text: The military has also shown its goodwill by issuing an order to the effect that hereafter all soldiers must pay fares on the trams. Last week the street railway represented to the government that because the soldiers rode free it was about to go into bankruptcy.

label: text
text: To-day "Young" Chang announced that he was moving his troops out as fast as possible. There are now about 24,000 troops in and immediately around Peking. He promises that within a week only one regiment will be in Peking, and one at the Temple of Heaven. The rest will be south-bound to aid Wu Pei-fu.

label: paragraph_title
text: NEWS AND NOT PUZZLES.

label: text
text: Home papers to hand are full of news from Hong Kong and China. At last, this Colony is getting the prominence it should, not through any fault of our own. But do the folks at Home comprehend the purport that is intended?

label: text
text: Here is one of the mysteries put to millions of readers of a London daily when the Wanhäsen rescue occupied pride of place:—“General Lieut. So-lung went over to the enemy.”

label: text
text: Evidence is not needed that narratives from the spot are welcome. Such news interests your friend. You can send no more welcome gift than the “Overland China Mail,” the weekly edition of all the local and Chinese news published daily, whether relating to Chinese or foreigners. It is the link with Hong Kong and compact enough to save a dozen letters.

label: text
text: But about this “General Lieut.” So little is known in the Old Country that names of places, generals, factions, organisations, &c., are sadly mutilated or misrepresented. The man referred to was Liu Tso-lung, who betrayed Wu Pei-fu and gave the Hanyang Arsenal to Canton.

label: text
text: The “China Mail” takes great pains in supplying footnotes and explanations to all messages which baffle the non-Chinese. A week's collection of these—in the “Overland”—make a handy reference for use here or abroad. Get a copy immediately!

label: text
text: This week has seen the momentous settlement of the boycott. Whatever views you hold individually, yours will be included as a complete record has been kept, making an excellent and readable narrative. All communiques, despatches and reports are reproduced. The first phase of what is hoped will be the new era of Hong Kong, is described in such a way as to be informative, convincing and impartial—thus meeting the requirements of all.

label: text
text: Every other bit of “local” news from last Thursday to this Wednesday inclusive will be found in this issue.
